BOW code: MOD-053

# Acceptance criteria — engine.social (MOD-053)

**BOW code:** MOD-053
**Spec refs:** §40 Social Services (`docs/METROPOLIS-MASTER-v2.1.md` lines 567-569: caseload generated by deprivation, unemployment duration, family stress (crowding + financial stress from §18), addiction (nightlife/deprivation coupling), and domestic-crisis events; provision: family support & child protection (underfunding shows up 10 years later as attainment down and crime up in the affected cohort — "the citizen records make this literal and auditable"), homelessness services (prevention + hostels + housing-first; failure = rough sleeping concentrated in the town centre, vitality down, "a person-shaped reproach in the ticker"), disability & carers support (releases informal carers back to workforce), fostering/adoption, addiction services (couples with §28 drug-crime generation — treatment cuts demand where policing cuts supply); "systemic role: social services set the floor of the Detroit spiral — a funded net makes decline shallower and recovery faster; a cut net turns recessions into collapses. Cheapest insurance in the game, easiest line to cut, longest fuse."); A5 the Slow-Fuse Principle (line 1367, binding across systems including — per this module's own code.json inbound pattern text — funding cuts); code.json `engine.social` entry (inbound `SocialAPI`, "caseload generation decomposed; **Slow-Fuse projections on cuts**", consumers: none registered; outbound calls `engine.services`, `engine.citizens`, `engine.wellbeing`, `engine.projections`).
**Date:** 2026-08-11 (BA-S9a, first pass)
**Status:** draft-ahead → dependencies closed — `MOD-018` (engine.citizens) and `MOD-033` (engine.services) are both `done`; the item is no longer held by its dependencies.
**Package under test:** `internal/engine/social/` (path from `node claude-bow.js show MOD-053`)
**Standard gates:** see `README.md` — all apply, package for SG-4/SG-7 is `./internal/engine/social/...`.

## User stories

- **US-1.** As deprivation, unemployment duration, family stress (crowding + financial stress, via `engine.wellbeing`'s registered drivers), and addiction pressure, I need to generate a real, typed caseload each month — not a single blended "social need" number — so each provision (family support, homelessness, disability/carers, fostering, addiction) has its own demand signal.
- **US-2.** As `engine.citizens` (a registered outbound dependency), I need caseload outcomes (a child-protection intervention, a fostering placement, a homelessness episode) written to the affected citizens' records through `CitizensAPI`'s command-based mutation path, so the "literal and auditable" cohort-outcome claim in §40 is a real, inspectable record, not a city-wide statistic with no traceable owner.
- **US-3.** As `engine.wellbeing` (a registered outbound dependency), I need `FinancialStress` and `Crowding` driver values (per `engine.wellbeing.md` AC-6) as this module's family-stress caseload input, so demand generation is not a second, duplicated stress model.
- **US-4.** As `engine.services` (a registered outbound dependency, MOD-033), I need social-worker staffing and funding to run through the shared service framework (capacity/coverage/funding→quality, per `engine.services.md` US-1), so a social-services budget cut is felt through the same mechanism as any other service cut.
- **US-5.** As the module's own code.json inbound pattern text states verbatim — "caseload generation decomposed; **Slow-Fuse projections on cuts**" — I need every funding-cut decision this module exposes to submit through `engine.projections`' Slow-Fuse gate with a real projected-consequence payload, exactly as this module's own registry entry already promises.
- **US-6.** As the Detroit-spiral system (`engine.spiral`, a later/other module, not owned here), I need this module's funded-vs-cut caseload outcomes queryable as a "floor" signal — a funded net shallower, a cut net steeper — so the spiral's own severity curve can eventually consume a real number rather than this module's narrative description of its own systemic role.
- **US-7.** As `engine.invariant`, I need every open case accounted for as a conserved stock the moment this module exists, so a case cannot silently close without a resolution, or vanish between categories during a referral.

## Scope

Per-category caseload generation (family support & child protection, homelessness, disability & carers, fostering/adoption, addiction services) from deprivation/unemployment-duration/family-stress/addiction/domestic-crisis-event drivers; provision effects (child-protection intervention outcomes written to citizen records, homelessness prevention/hostel/housing-first mechanics, informal-carer workforce release, fostering placement, addiction treatment coupled with §28); the funding→quality path via `engine.services`; submission of funding-cut decisions to `engine.projections`' Slow-Fuse gate; caseload conservation accounting as a new invariant-checker stock.

## Acceptance criteria

### Functional — caseload generation, decomposed

- **AC-1 (GR#20; code.json inbound contract).** A `SocialAPI` exists exposing per-category caseload queries and funding-level mutation commands, matching code.json's documented pattern "caseload generation decomposed; Slow-Fuse projections on cuts". Check: `go doc ./internal/engine/social SocialAPI` shows both a per-category query surface and a command-based funding mutation; `grep -n "func.*SetFunding" internal/engine/social/*.go` confirms funding changes are commands, not public field writes.
- **AC-2 (§40 five distinct provision categories; "decomposed" is binding, not incidental).** Caseload is tracked separately for at least the five named categories — family support & child protection, homelessness, disability & carers, fostering/adoption, addiction services — each independently queryable, each responding to a documented subset of the drivers (not all five sharing one blended demand number). Check: `go doc ./internal/engine/social` shows five distinct category accessors; a passing test raises exactly one driver (e.g. unemployment duration) and asserts it measurably increases at least one category's caseload while leaving a category the spec does not couple to that driver (e.g. disability & carers, which §40 does not tie to unemployment duration) materially unchanged (`grep -rn "func Test.*[Cc]ategory[Ii]solat\|func Test.*[Dd]ecomposedCaseload" internal/engine/social/*_test.go`). **Lazy implementation this rejects — the exact failure the code.json pattern string's word "decomposed" exists to prevent:** a single weighted-sum "social need" score with five display labels computed by proportional split (the same shape AC-3 of `engine.wellbeing.md` rejects for driver attribution) would satisfy "five categories exist" on a shallow read while making every category move together on any driver change — this AC's isolation check is the load-bearing half, directly modelled on `engine.wellbeing.md` AC-3's precedent.
- **AC-3 (§40 family-stress driver; GR#20 outbound contract).** Family-stress caseload input is sourced from `engine.wellbeing`'s registered `Crowding` and `FinancialStress` driver values (per `engine.wellbeing.md` AC-6, including that module's documented 35%-rent-burden threshold behaviour) via the registered `WellbeingAPI`, never a locally-duplicated crowding/rent-burden computation. Check: `grep -rn "wellbeing\.(Crowding|FinancialStress)" internal/engine/social/*.go` (excluding `_test.go`) shows a live call into `engine.wellbeing`'s exported drivers; a passing test asserts changing a citizen's rent burden across `engine.wellbeing`'s 35% threshold changes this module's family-stress caseload input without this package independently re-deriving rent burden from raw rent/income figures (`grep -rn "func Test.*[Ff]amilyStress" internal/engine/social/*_test.go`).
- **AC-4 (§40 addiction coupling with §28; GR#20 outbound-edge status — see Escalations).** Addiction-services caseload demand is coupled to nightlife/deprivation drivers per §40, and addiction treatment funding is documented as reducing the demand side of §28's drug-crime-supply loop ("treatment cuts demand where policing cuts supply") — but this AC's *demand-side* half only, since no `engine.social`↔`engine.crime` edge is registered in code.json for the *supply-side* coupling (flagged in Escalations, not blocking this AC since the demand-side mechanic is self-contained within this module). Check: `go doc ./internal/engine/social` shows an addiction-caseload accessor responsive to a deprivation/nightlife-density input; a passing test asserts raising deprivation increases addiction-services caseload demand (`grep -rn "func Test.*[Aa]ddiction" internal/engine/social/*_test.go`).
- **AC-5 (§40 domestic-crisis events).** Domestic-crisis events (discrete, per-household triggerable events, not a smooth background rate) generate an immediate family-support/child-protection caseload spike distinct from the steady-state deprivation/unemployment-driven baseline, and each event is independently traceable (not folded anonymously into the monthly aggregate). Check: `go doc ./internal/engine/social` shows a discrete crisis-event constructor/handler distinct from the steady-state generator; a passing test injects one crisis event and asserts a traceable caseload entry appears attributable to that specific event, not merely a city-wide count increment (`grep -rn "func Test.*[Cc]risisEvent" internal/engine/social/*_test.go`).

### Functional — provision effects and cohort auditability

- **AC-6 (§40 "literal and auditable"; the core cohort-outcome mechanism, checkable without a 10-year run).** A child-protection intervention (or its absence, under sustained underfunding) writes a documented marker to the affected citizen's record via `CitizensAPI`'s command path (per `engine.citizens.md` AC-1b) **at the time of the intervention decision**, not deferred — so the eventual "attainment down and crime up... 10 years later" claim is traceable back to a real, dated record entry from the day it happened, exactly mirroring `engine.education.md`'s AC-6 pattern for the same class of long-fuse claim. Check: `go doc ./internal/engine/social` shows an intervention-marker write call at the point of decision; a passing test constructs an underfunded-family-support scenario, asserts a documented marker is written to the affected citizen's record immediately (measured at the same simulated month, no elapsed time required), and that the marker is queryable through `CitizensAPI` by a hypothetical later consumer without re-deriving it (`grep -rn "func Test.*[Ii]nterventionMarker\|func Test.*[Cc]ohortAudit" internal/engine/social/*_test.go`). **Lazy implementation this rejects:** a module that only tracks aggregate "cases handled this month" without writing anything to the individual citizen record would satisfy "child protection exists" while making §40's explicit "literal and auditable... in citizen records" claim false — the check requires the record-level write, not an aggregate count.
- **AC-7 (§40 homelessness pipeline).** Homelessness has three documented, distinct states/paths — prevention (intercepts a caseload entry before street homelessness occurs), hostel placement (temporary, capacity-limited via `engine.services`), and housing-first (a policy-gated direct-to-housing path, per §40's explicit naming) — and failure across all three (capacity exhausted, prevention declined/unavailable, housing-first not enacted) results in a queryable rough-sleeping count concentrated at a specific location (town centre, per spec) rather than a diffuse city-wide statistic, feeding a documented vitality penalty. Check: `go doc ./internal/engine/social` shows distinct accessors for the three paths and a location-attributed rough-sleeping count; a passing test exhausts hostel capacity and disables housing-first, and asserts the rough-sleeping count rises and is attributed to the documented town-centre location (`grep -rn "func Test.*[Hh]omelessness" internal/engine/social/*_test.go`).
- **AC-8 (§40 disability & carers workforce release).** Funded disability & carers support produces a queryable "informal carers released to workforce" figure — a real labour-supply effect, not a satisfaction-only description — exported for a future consumer (`engine.firms`/`engine.citizens` employment matching, out of scope here). Check: `go doc ./internal/engine/social` shows a carers-released accessor; a passing test asserts increasing disability & carers funding increases the released-carers figure at fixed caseload (`grep -rn "func Test.*[Cc]arersReleased" internal/engine/social/*_test.go`).
- **AC-9 (§40 fostering/adoption).** Fostering placements are tracked as a distinct caseload category from child protection generally (§40 names it separately), with placement capacity gated via `engine.services` and a documented match/no-match outcome per placement attempt (never an unconditional "placed" result regardless of capacity). Check: `go doc ./internal/engine/social` shows a fostering-placement accessor distinct from the general child-protection category; a passing test exhausts foster-placement capacity and asserts a subsequent placement attempt returns a documented no-match/queued state, not a silently-succeeded placement (`grep -rn "func Test.*[Ff]osterCapacity" internal/engine/social/*_test.go`).

### Functional — the Slow-Fuse obligation (the module's own registry-stated contract)

- **AC-10 (US-5; the module's own code.json pattern text, "Slow-Fuse projections on cuts" — RE-ARMED 2026-08-11, BUG-100: the `engine.social`→`engine.projections` edge landed in c36778b).** Every funding-*cut* command (a `SetFunding` call reducing a category's current funding level) is submitted through `engine.projections`' generic Slow-Fuse gate (`engine.projections.md` AC-5) with a real projected-consequence payload — this is not an inference from spec prose the way `engine.education`'s AC-9 is; it is the literal, verbatim text of this module's own code.json inbound `pattern` field, and the edge now backs it: `node -e "const m=require('./code.json').modules.find(x=>x.key==='engine.social'); process.exit(m.outbound.calls.some(c=>c.key==='engine.projections')?0:1)"` exits 0. The registry is no longer self-contradicting for this module. A funding-cut command must carry a `FuseYears` tag, compute a local projected-consequence value, AND make the real cross-module submission call — deferring the submission is no longer legal now the path exists. Check: `grep -n "FuseYears" internal/engine/social/*.go` shows funding-cut commands carry the tag; a passing test asserts a funding-cut command without an attached local projection value is rejected by this module's own pre-submission check (`grep -rn "func Test.*[Ss]lowFuse.*[Cc]ut\|func Test.*[Ff]useYears" internal/engine/social/*_test.go`); `grep -n "projections\.RegisterCurveProvider\|projections\.Submit" internal/engine/social/*.go` (excluding `_test.go`) shows the real submission call — its absence FAILS this AC; `doc.go` no longer cites BUG-058 as a live block for AC-10.

### Functional — conservation identity (the caseload stock)

- **AC-11 (case-accounting identity — the strongest available check).** For every category and every accounting month, the following identity holds exactly: `OpenCases == OpenCasesLastMonth + NewCasesOpened(from AC-2/AC-5's independent generators) − CasesResolved(closed with a documented outcome) − CasesEscalated(closed in this category but reopened as a linked, traceable case in another category — e.g. an unresolved family-support case escalating to child protection — never a silent close with no paired reopen) − CasesLostToFollowUp(a documented, flagged fallback state — citizen relocated/untraceable — never a silent drop)`. Every term is independently sourced (opened from the generators, resolved/escalated/lost from this module's own case-closure log, with an escalation requiring the paired reopen event to exist in the destination category's own `NewCasesOpened` count) — none is the identity's remainder. Check: a passing test runs a synthetic caseload through several months with a mix of resolutions, one cross-category escalation, and one lost-to-follow-up, independently sums each term from its own source, and asserts the sum reconciles exactly per category per month, with the escalation specifically checked to appear as both a closure in the source category and an open in the destination category in the same month (`grep -rn "func Test.*[Cc]aseConserv\|func Test.*[Cc]aseloadIdentity" internal/engine/social/*_test.go`). **Lazy implementation this rejects:** closing a case as "resolved" when it was actually abandoned/lost to follow-up (the path of least resistance for a caseworker-simulation implementation under time pressure to show a clean closure rate) would make the identity balance while silently misrepresenting the service's real effectiveness — precisely the kind of number a funding debate would be having an argument over the wrong evidence for. The check's escalation-pairing requirement additionally catches a case "disappearing" from one category without a corresponding appearance in another, which a naive open/close count alone would not.
- **AC-12 (US-7; registration with `engine.invariant` — STILL BLOCKED after c36778b; BUG-100 tripwire applied).** The caseload-accounting identity (AC-11) is registered as a conserved stock with `engine.invariant`'s registration seam. **Blocked — the `engine.social`→`engine.invariant` edge remains unregistered (BUG-058 and BUG-067 are both `done`, but neither added this edge).** code.json still shows no `engine.social`→`engine.invariant` outbound edge as of c36778b (that commit registered `engine.social`→`engine.projections`, not this edge); `engine.invariant`'s inbound contract is populated only by `engine.citizens`/`engine.finance`/`engine.traffic`. BUG-067's closure shipped `RegisterStockWithTerms`, so the multi-term-identity API blocker is gone — what remains is the unregistered edge plus an open question of whether the caseload stock needs its own registration or is subsumed under `engine.citizens`' people-stock (Aaron ruling, see Escalations). AC-11's local test suite is the interim proof of correctness. **Tripwire (mechanical, not a prose label — BUG-100):** `node -e "const m=require('./code.json').modules.find(x=>x.key==='engine.social'); process.exit(m.outbound.calls.some(c=>c.key==='engine.invariant')?1:0)"` must exit **0** (edge still absent). A nonzero exit means the edge has landed and this AC is stale, unarmed prose that MUST be rewritten to the real check before the next commit touching `internal/engine/social/`; Tester/CI treat a nonzero exit here as a hard FAIL, not a silent pass. Until the tripwire fires: once unblocked, `grep -n "invariant\.Register" internal/engine/social/*.go` shows registration at boot; until then, `doc.go` states the block, citing the missing `engine.social`→`engine.invariant` edge rather than a since-closed BUG-058.

### Error handling

- **AC-13 (GR#7).** A funding command targeting an unregistered category, or a case-query for an unregistered case ID, returns a registry-sourced error (new `MET-E`-range code, claimed at build time — no `engine.social` sub-range exists yet), never a silently-created zero-value case. Check: `grep -n "MET-" internal/engine/social/*.go` finds a registry code reference; passing test coverage (`grep -rn "func Test.*[Uu]nregisteredCategory\|func Test.*[Uu]nknownCase" internal/engine/social/*_test.go`) — **GR#7 assertion, stated explicitly (BUG-100):** the test asserts the returned error's registry code matches AND that no zero-value case record was created, not merely that a matching-named test function exists.
- **AC-14.** An escalation command naming a destination category that does not exist, or a resolution command for a case already closed, is rejected with a typed error, never silently accepted with the identity quietly drifting. Check: passing test coverage (`grep -rn "func Test.*[Ii]nvalidEscalation\|func Test.*[Dd]oubleClose" internal/engine/social/*_test.go`).

### Determinism, safety & scale

- **AC-15 (GR#21).** Caseload generation, provision matching (hostel/foster placement), and escalation routing are deterministic functions of `(worldSeed, tick, prior state, commands)` via the counter-based hash stream, byte-identical across repeated runs and worker counts; where a shortage forces a priority order (e.g. limited hostel beds across multiple pending cases), the order is a documented, deterministic rule, never map-iteration order. Check: `grep -n "for .* := range" internal/engine/social/*.go` on any map feeding allocation order is sorted (`grep -n "sort\." internal/engine/social/*.go`); a passing determinism test exists (`grep -rn "func Test.*[Dd]eterminis" internal/engine/social/*_test.go`).
- **AC-16 (SG-7; GR#21).** `grep -rn "time.Now\|time.Since" internal/engine/social/*.go` (excluding `_test.go`) returns no matches.
- **AC-17.** `go test ./internal/engine/social/... -race -count=1` passes; `grep -n "go func()" internal/engine/social/*_test.go` finds at least one concurrency test (concurrent caseload updates across categories within a tick).

### Documentation

- **AC-18.** `internal/engine/social/doc.go` states the module key `engine.social`, cites §40, states the case-accounting identity (AC-11) in prose with every term named including the escalation-pairing rule, states the one remaining unregistered edge (AC-12's invariant edge) explicitly — AC-10's projections edge is now registered (c36778b), and states the five decomposed provision categories (AC-2) so a future reader does not collapse them into one blended score. Check: `grep -n "engine.social" internal/engine/social/doc.go` and `grep -n "§40\|section 40" internal/engine/social/doc.go` both match; `grep -n "engine.invariant" internal/engine/social/doc.go` matches (the AC-12 block statement); `grep -n "BUG-058" internal/engine/social/doc.go` returns no matches (BUG-058 and BUG-067 are closed).

## Out of scope

- `engine.wellbeing`'s own driver-decomposition mechanics — this item only consumes `Crowding`/`FinancialStress` (AC-3).
- `engine.services`' own capacity/coverage/funding→quality function and staffing-pool mechanics — this item registers against it (AC-4/AC-7/AC-9) but does not reimplement it.
- §28's crime-generation side of the addiction demand/supply coupling, and any `engine.crime` edge that coupling would require — flagged in Escalations, not built here.
- `engine.spiral`'s own Detroit-spiral severity curve — this item exposes a funded-vs-cut floor signal (US-6) for a future consumer; it does not compute spiral severity itself.
- `engine.projections`' own Slow-Fuse gate mechanics — this item only submits to it (AC-10; the `engine.social`→`engine.projections` edge landed in c36778b).
- `engine.firms`/`engine.citizens`' consumption of the carers-released labour-supply figure (AC-8) — exported here, consumed elsewhere.
- Specific caseload-generation rates, hostel/foster capacity figures, and the crisis-event trigger probability — balance data pending M2 tuning (see Escalations).

## Escalations

- **For Ben — BUG-058/BUG-067 closure refresh (2026-08-16).** The `engine.social`→`engine.projections` edge this file's AC-10 flagged has landed (c36778b); AC-10 is re-armed. BUG-058 closed 2026-08-13 (18 spec-traced edges added) and BUG-067 closed 2026-08-14 (`RegisterStockWithTerms`), but `engine.social`→`engine.invariant` was NOT among the added edges — so AC-12's block is now the unregistered edge itself plus the open question of whether the caseload stock needs its own registration vs. subsumption under `engine.citizens`' people-stock (Aaron ruling). The `engine.social`↔`engine.crime` addiction-treatment/§28-drug-supply coupling is likewise unchanged: AC-4's demand-side-only scoping works around it without an edge, but the supply-side half remains unregistered and unbuildable.
- **For Aaron (balance numbers, ASM candidate).** Caseload-generation rates per driver unit, hostel/foster/carers capacity figures, and the domestic-crisis event trigger probability are none of them spec-given magnitudes — §40 gives mechanism and systemic framing only. ACs above check decomposition/isolation/direction (per GR#15); actual figures are `data/social.json` (or equivalent) balance data pending M2 tuning. Filing as an assumption if a junior needs a placeholder before Aaron rules: `node claude-bow.js add assumption "social-services caseload generation rates and provision-capacity figures are placeholder until M2 balance pass" --priority P2 --code-path internal/engine/social --codejson engine.social --desc "Spec gives driver list and systemic role (§40) but no magnitudes for caseload-per-driver-unit, hostel/foster/carers capacity, or crisis-event probability. Needed a number to write a compiling junior build; without Aaron's ruling the placeholder risks becoming de facto balance by inertia."`
- **For Ben (dependency risk — resolved by closure).** This item depends on `MOD-018` (citizens) and `MOD-033` (services), both now `done`, so the real `CitizensAPI`/`WellbeingAPI`/`ServicesAPI` shapes AC-3/AC-6/AC-7 rely on are available; the earlier stub-first recommendation no longer applies.
- **Assumption logged — ASM-1342 (P2, directional balance data).** `data/social.json`'s caseload-generation rates, hostel/foster/carers capacities, crisis cases-per-event, and the intervention-harm threshold are all placeholders pending the M2 balance pass (balance-number regime, GR#15); §40 gives mechanism and framing only, no magnitudes.
- **Assumption logged — ASM-1364 (P2, balance-shaped model simplification).** Hostel and foster stays are modelled as one-month occupancy (capacity = per-month placements, released each new routing/placement month); §40 specifies no stay duration, so the one-month default is a balance-regime placeholder — a longer real stay length is an M2 balance concern, not a mechanism defect (SEC-178's release requirement holds regardless).
- **Assumption logged — ASM-1382 (P1, finite-guard resource ceiling).** `maxCaseloadProposalsPerMonth=100000` is a SEC-195 resource ceiling bounding the per-month proposal count, not a player-felt balance number; the value is a placeholder sitting well above shipped `data/social.json` rates and below attack magnitudes, pending Aaron/M2 review.
